title: Keel's Integration Boost partners receive near-identical terms, so partnership negotiation is standardized rather than bespoke
content:
Comparing the five Integration Boost Instances parameter by parameter, the differences are almost nil. Each is weekly (e.g. A.6.1.1.3.2.5.2.2.3.1.4, …4.1.4, …3.1.1.4); each names the Core Council Risk Advisor as Data Submission Responsible Actor; each points at the same Blockanalitica `solana-incentives` endpoint; each states the boost is "calculated based on per block values for USDS in [venue] and the Sky Savings Rate"; and each Agent Customizations slot reads "[No customization presently.]"

What varies is only partner name, chain, and reward address. In other words, the Instance-per-partner structure from the Primitive design is being used to hold a *standard contract*, not to express negotiated variation.

That is a meaningful commercial posture. A venue joining Keel's boost program takes published terms it cannot bargain over, which removes the most-favoured-nation problem entirely: no partner can discover it received worse economics than a competitor, because the economics are formula-driven from the same rate gap and measured by the same third party.

The standardization also lowers Keel's own operating cost — one measurement pipeline, one cadence, one review rhythm across every venue — at the price of flexibility. A partner that would only integrate on non-standard terms cannot currently be accommodated without filling in a customization slot that has, so far, never been used.
description: Across Kamino, Drift, Save, Lifinity and MarginFi the cadence, measurement actor, data endpoint, savings-rate strategy and empty customization slot are the same;
